title: 5.5.1: Exercises
originalText:
Exercise \(\PageIndex{1}\)

Plot each point in a rectangular coordinate system and identify the quadrant in which the point is located.

1. \((3, -1)\)

2. \((-3, 1)\)

3. \((-2, 0)\)

4. \((-4, -3)\)

5. \((1,\frac14{5})\)

For each ordered pair below, decide:

1. Is the ordered pair a solution to the equation?

2. Is the point on the line in the given graph?

\(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\)

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 8 to 8, in increments of 1. The line passes through the points, (negative 6, negative 6), (0, negative 3), and (6, 0).]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{2}\)

\(\left( {0,-3} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{3}\)

\(\left( {2,-2} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{4}\)

\(\left( {-2,-4} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{5}\)

\(\left( {4,1} \right)\)

For each ordered pair below, decide:

1. Is the ordered pair a solution to the equation?

2. Is the point on the line in the given graph?

\(y = x - 4\)

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 8 to 8, in increments of 1. The line passes through the points, (negative 3, negative 7), (0, negative 4), (4, 0), and (7, 3).]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{6}\)

\(\left( {0,-4} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{7}\)

\(\left( {3,-1} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{8}\)

\(\left( {2,2} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{9}\)

\(\left( {1,-5} \right)\)

For each ordered pair below, decide:

1. Is the ordered pair a solution to the equation?

2. Is the point on the line in the given graph?

\(y = \frac{1}{3}x + 2\)

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 8 to 8, in increments of 1. The line passes through the points, (negative 6, 0), (0, 2), and (6, 4).]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{10}\)

\(\left( {0,2} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{11}\)

\(\left( {3,3} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{12}\)

\(\left( {-3,2} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{13}\)

\(\left( {-6,0} \right)\)

For the following exercises, graph by plotting points.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{14}\)

\(y = 3x - 1\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{15}\)

\(y = -x - 3\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{16}\)

\(y = 2x\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{17}\)

\(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{18}\)

\(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 5\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{19}\)

\(y = \frac{2}{5}x + 1\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{20}\)

\(y = \frac{3}{2}x + 2\)

For the following exercises, determine whether each ordered pair is a solution to the inequality.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{21}\)

\(y>x-3\)

A: \((0,0) \quad\) B: \((2,1) \quad\) C: \((-1,-5) \quad\) D: \((-6,-3) \quad\) E: \((1,0)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{22}\)

\(y<3 x+2\)

A: \((0,3) \quad\) B: \((-3,-2) \quad\) C: \((-2,0) \quad\) D: \((0,0) \quad\) E: \((-1,4)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{23}\)

\(y<-2 x+5\)

\(\mathrm{A}:(-3,0) \quad \mathrm{B}:(1,6) \quad \mathrm{C}:(-6,-2) \quad \mathrm{D}:(0,1) \quad \mathrm{E}:(5,-4)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{24}\)

\(3 x-4 y>4\)

A: \((5,1) \quad \mathrm{B}:(-2,6) \quad \mathrm{C}:(3,2) \quad \mathrm{D}:(10,-5) \quad \mathrm{E}:(0,0)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{25}\)

\(2 x+3 y>2\)

\(\mathrm{A}:(1,1) \quad \mathrm{B}:(4,-3) \quad \mathrm{C}:(0,0) \quad \mathrm{D}:(-8,12) \quad \mathrm{E}:(3,0)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{26}\)

Write the inequality shown by the graph with the boundary line \(y=3 x-4\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (0, negative 5), (2.5, 2.5), and (5, 10). The region to the right of the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{27}\)

Write the inequality shown by the graph with the boundary line \(y = 2x - 4\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (0, negative 5), (2.5, 0), and (5, 5). The region to the right of the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{28}\)

Write the inequality shown by the graph with the boundary line \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 1\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (negative 7.5, negative 2.5), (0, 1), and (7.5, 5). The region below the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{29}\)

Write the inequality shown by the graph with the boundary line \(y = - \frac{1}{3}x - 2\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (negative 10, 1), (negative 5, 0), (0, negative 2.3), and (10, negative 5). The region below the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{30}\)

Write the inequality shown by the shaded region in the graph with the boundary line \(\;x + y = 5\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (negative 5, 10), (0, 5), (5, 0), and (10, negative 5). The region above the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{31}\)

Write the inequality shown by the shaded region in the graph with the boundary line \(x + y = 3\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (negative 5, 7.5), (0, 3), (2.5, 0), and (10, negative 7). The region above the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{32}\)

Write the inequality shown by the shaded region in the graph with the boundary line \(3x - y = 6\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (negative 1, negative 10), (2.3, 0), and (5, 10). The region to the left of the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{33}\)

Write the inequality shown by the shaded region in the graph with the boundary line \(2x - y = 4\).

[Figure: A line is plotted on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes range from negative 10 to 10, in increments of 2.5. The line passes through the points, (negative 2.5, negative 10), (2.5, 0), and (7, 10). The region to the left of the line is shaded. Note: all values are approximate.]

For the following exercises, graph the linear inequality.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{34}\)

\(y < \frac{3}{5}x + 2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{35}\)

\(y \leq - \frac{1}{2}x + 4\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{36}\)

\(y \geq - \frac{1}{3}x - 2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{37}\)

\(x - y \leq 3\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{38}\)

\(x - y \geq - 2\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{39}\)

\(4x + y > - 4\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{40}\)

\(x + 5y < - 5\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{41}\)

\(3x + 2y \geq - 6\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{42}\)

\(4x + 2y \geq - 8\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{43}\)

\(y > 4x\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{44}\)

\(y \leq - 3x\)
